original_test_intent: Validate that the BMC OEM firmware WebUI can program the approved DC-SCM FPGA image, preserve the requested configuration, expose the correct resulting FPGA firmware version, and leave the platform free of unexpected system or management logs.
original_method: On the specified SUT, bind an approved signed/hash-verified DC-SCM FPGA .ima to the exact board/FRU/device and expected current/target version, capture configuration, FPGA identity/version, BMC/host health and cleared-log timestamps, perform the BMC OEM WebUI flash under stable power and OOB supervision without interruption, activate/reset only as approved, then verify the active device/version, retained configuration, health, photos and log delta.
manual_activity: A firmware owner identifies the physical DC-SCM and recoverable programming path, approves the image and target version, observes the critical programming/activation interval, and confirms the photographed/result evidence belongs to that device.
required_inputs: Approved DC-SCM FPGA .ima with origin, version, cryptographic hash/signature and release notes
DC-SCM board/FRU/revision and FPGA device identity mapped to current/target versions
BMC OEM endpoint, secure credentials and UI access
Stable power, OOB console, backup, golden-image or hardware recovery instructions
Expected post-test log policy and artifact destination
safety_requirements: Confirm the OEM target resolves to the intended DC-SCM FPGA before upload
Maintain stable power and management connectivity throughout erase/program/verify/activation
Never bypass compatibility, signature or rollback controls
Stop on identity mismatch, validation failure, task error, thermal/power fault or lost OOB visibility
Do not automatically retry a failed FPGA programming operation
Preserve timestamped pre/post logs, UI evidence and recovery state
agent_execution_scope: May validate an owner-approved manifest, capture read-only identity/version/log baselines, assist the exact OEM WebUI workflow under supervision, monitor task state and gather post-update evidence

Must not infer the target FPGA from an OEM label, choose or transform an image, use a generic Redfish endpoint as an unapproved substitute, decide activation/reset policy, retry failure or declare DUT PASS
engineer_actions: Approve the image-to-DC-SCM hardware compatibility and expected version
Define configuration preservation, activation/reset and acceptable log behavior
Verify OOB/golden-image or hardware recovery readiness and supervise programming
Review the active post-update identity/version and assign the hardware verdict

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: A generic Redfish UpdateService POST is only an implementation candidate: the source calls for the OEM firmware WebUI, and a generic service may address a different inventory member or omit the UI coverage.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Retain the BMC OEM WebUI path and bind the upload to the owner-approved DC-SCM device/image manifest. Use an API only when its exact OEM target mapping and coverage equivalence are approved and recorded.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: DC-SCM FPGA target, .ima upload, Preserve all Configuration choice, before/during/after phases, result/photo collection and unexpected-log inspection remain in scope.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Create an immutable preflight ledger for board/FRU/FPGA identity, image hash and expected active version; record OEM task phases and device-specific activation, then reconcile active version, configuration, platform health and log deltas against that ledger.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds device-level target binding, cryptographic provenance, task/activation evidence, fail-closed controls and recovery readiness while retaining the original OEM WebUI flow and artifacts.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: No reduction when the OEM WebUI is exercised; a generic Redfish-only execution cannot be credited for the UI workflow or device selection without approved equivalence.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Programming the wrong programmable device or losing power can require board-level recovery; a version string cached by BMC may not prove the running FPGA image, so reset/activation and identity must be established.

project_override_considerations: The platform team must provide the DC-SCM FRU/revision matrix, FPGA device/version inventory mapping, signed image, OEM update behavior, reset/activation sequence, log allowlist and recovery ownership.
expected_evidence: Approved image manifest and DC-SCM board/FRU/FPGA compatibility map
Pre-update physical/logical target identity, active version, configuration and health
Timestamped BMC OEM WebUI selection, upload, erase/program/verify and completion evidence
Approved activation/reset trace and active post-update FPGA version tied to the same device
Configuration comparison, required photos/results, host/BMC health and unexpected-log delta
Abort, rollback or hardware-recovery evidence when applicable

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The source, DeepSeek and GPT V2 agree on a DC-SCM FPGA firmware flash requiring an approved .ima and version verification; the API suggestion is treated as conditional rather than authoritative replacement.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The static review is complete; execution is conditional on the project image, exact device mapping, credentials, activation policy and recovery controls.

review_improvement: Makes the OEM firmware target device-specific, preserves UI and log coverage, distinguishes staged/cached metadata from an active FPGA image, and prevents unsafe image choice, interruption and retry.
independent_technical_reasoning: DC-SCM can contain multiple programmable or managed components, so an OEM update success message is not sufficient evidence that the intended FPGA was programmed. The proof chain must bind physical FRU and FPGA identity to the approved bitstream, programming task, activation event and active post-reset version while also checking platform logs for collateral faults.
